items.title: Show HN: Babeltro – Nine demoscene effects in 13 languages, pixel-identical
items.summary: I was wondering how those classic demoscene effects come out in different languages. It’s interesting to see the required contortions for each language to get there. For example, SQLite has no float32, so it's emulated in SQL. Wasm has no sin(), so the hand-written port builds its own sine table, to name a few. It was built end-to-end by AI agents. Every port is checked pixel by pixel against the C reference by a script in the repo.

Show HN: Extending X402 for MoR fiat payments and budget attenuation
items.summary: X402 and similar protocols requires crypto native settlement. For freelancers and SMEs under many European tax regimes, it can be a tax nightmare. In this proposal the payment is in FIAT (via a Merchant of Record), and the agents orchestrator can attenuate the budget into smaller, independently revocable sub-budgets for its worker using Biscuits. This is a reference implementation with some described known limitations, not a production system. I'd love to get feedback. Thanks for taking a look!

Show HN: Render your Windows desktop GUI on the NPU
items.summary: Hi HN, a kind of funny project we've been hacking on for a couple of weeks. We wanted to see if it was possible to get Windows into using the NPU like a GPU, and compositing the desktop GUI. Why? Well the longer-term idea is to free up the GPU as much as possible so eventually, you could have more GPU free for AI inference. By offloading the work to the NPU we did manage to bring 3D GPU usage down from 3.4% to 0.6%... but at a large expense to performance (you will get 1.6 FPS doing this). Show HN: Calltags, an Android dialer for people without contact lists
items.summary: The idea is that you get a call history and you can label calls and later search or browse them to find numbers. Contact lists are bloated and made for a different time. These days just some plain labels on numbers should be enough. This approach doesn't discriminate between contacts that are worth adding to a canonical "list of contacts" and people or institutions that have called you only once: everybody can get a label the same way. I've wanted an app like this to exist for a long time, but never found it, so now I can finally be happy with my sporadic use of the phone dialer again.
items.company: Calltags, an Android dialer for people without contact lists
